Rules written before reading: a pair counts only if its first part, read whole, calls for or proposes an attack; others are set aside and counted. An account is a clause in the reply giving a reason or ground for its stance: a because, since or so clause; a stated rule or norm; a fact offered as a ground (allies, first there, their flag); a consequence. A bare assent, a bare refusal, a directive with no ground, a joke or a report of action is not an account. Prediction: refusals carry an account more often than acceptances and are longer.
